findings.description: __aexit__ discards the actual exception arguments and calls self.__exit__(None, None, None), so the AttemptManager never sees the exception raised inside the async with block.
findings.rationale: Trigger: an exception is raised inside `async with attempt:` (e.g., a failed I/O call). The sync __exit__ is designed to receive exc_type/exc_value to call set_exception on the retry state; passing None makes it record a successful result instead. Mechanism: the failure is silently swallowed and set_result(None) is recorded, so the retry loop believes the attempt succeeded and never retries. Impact: retries are silently skipped and failed operations are reported as successful, a silent wrong result.
